description: Index of every built-in Ferrum Edge plugin at v0.9.21: name, registration failure policy, documented priority, phases and protocol surface, and a pointer to the plugin's config schema in Edge's published openapi.yaml. Build-time custom plugins are not listed.

provenance.note: v0.9.21 retains the 82 registered types, two removed names, response-body producer and WebSocket framing membership, and every PluginConfigBase pointer, config-required and scope conditional. Registration failure policies and parity metadata are re-transcribed from the tag: http_logging, udp_logging, statsd_logging, loki_logging and ws_frame_logging move from optional_fail_open to keep_last_known_good (Edge #7369); http_logging, tcp_logging, kafka_logging, loki_logging and udp_logging add on_ws_disconnect (Edge #7369); request_transformer adds on_final_request_body_with_context and response_transformer adds finalize_client_visible_response_body (Edge #7469); and compression adds zstd to its protocol_rationale. Referenced OpenAPI config components ship the v0.9.21 removed keys, managed jwks_source, mesh_route_dispatch weighted_splits, mesh_authz node_waypoint_route_branches, plugin trigger external_identity/external_identity_authority predicates, access_control authority binding, request_mirror allow_plaintext, loopback-IP cleartext rules, chargeback 1.0e+288 bounds, OIDC canonical redirects, and A2A fail-closed classification recorded in docs/plugin-config-admission.md.

config_schema_document.note: Each config_schema.pointer is a JSON Pointer into this exact file. The schemas are OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON Schema 2020-12 dialect) and may $ref other components in the same document. They apply to `config` only when the plugin config is enabled. ci/plugin_config_schemas.py also publishes each pointer's schema, with every component it references, as a standalone JSON Schema 2020-12 document in plugin-config-schemas/<plugin>.schema.json, generated from this exact file; CI checks the generated files against it.

protocol_values.http: HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, including HTTPS
protocol_values.tcp: Raw TCP stream proxy, including TLS termination and origination
protocol_values.udp: Raw UDP datagram proxy, including DTLS termination and origination

main_branch_delta.summary: No plugin registration, removed-plugin, failure-policy, parity, protocol or config_schema pointer changes beyond v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3) at Edge main e333ba3fe51ffed19ce3b0a53140ba4340707589 (through Edge PR #7533, the 1.0.0 release-notes refresh on top of Edge PR #7531, which prepares version 1.0.0; untagged). src/plugins/builtin_parity.rs is byte-identical to v0.9.21; src/plugins/mod.rs changes only internal hot-path helpers (Edge #7471 and #7474), the type of RequestContext.timestamp_received (chrono DateTime<Utc> to time_compat::UtcTimestamp, Edge #7518; custom-plugin Rust API, not a wire change) and the orig_dst field documentation (Edge #7520), with BUILTIN_PLUGIN_REGISTRATIONS, REMOVED_PLUGIN_REGISTRATIONS, ProxyProtocol, failure policies and parity values identical to v0.9.21. Unreleased plugin config admission outside openapi.yaml (Edge #7511, #7512, #7513, #7516; issue #7419): parsed timestamps are UTC instants in years -9999..=9999 with a leap second stored as the following second, so a transaction_debugger capture_expires_at that v0.9.21 accepted but that falls outside that range in UTC (for example 9999-12-31T23:30:00-01:00) is now refused, response_caching treats such an HTTP date as unparseable, and soap_ws_security refuses such an instant (a 9999-12-31T23:59:60Z leap second is out of range). openapi.yaml moves to SHA-256 145067e5b04161ad2bd8145856139a609744c4d804c2501fdc94cdb3f3cd5370 with info.version 1.0.0 (Edge #7531; it was cc6f0a7ee6cff646e50f6a12a13211a781fb5574dcdf116a0b394355b5fbf532 at Edge main e837270d4b6c1c9756b80400d2a8e2e14b176ce4 after Edge #7491). Of the components reachable from PluginConfigBase and every plugin config_schema pointer, only two change: PluginConfigBase gains additionalProperties: false (Edge #7524), which states in the schema that the top-level plugin config object refuses unknown members as it already did at runtime in v0.9.21, with its required list, properties and every per-plugin if/then conditional (config_schema pointer, config_required_when_enabled, scope_constraint) unchanged; and AiSemanticCacheConfig changes description text only (Edge #7531). Plugin config objects stay open to each plugin's own validation. Unreleased Admin and API-spec rules outside plugin config schemas (Edge #7520 and #7524): proxy plugins[] associations (PluginAssociation) refuse members other than plugin_config_id with 400 on the Admin API, /batch, file mode and in the typed proxies of POST /restore (which refuses the whole backup before restoring anything), and POST/PUT /api-specs refuse an x-ferrum-proxy or x-ferrum-upstream extension carrying an unknown nested key or such an association member, while a stored spec document is projected onto plugin_config_id so a historical member never blocks the replacing PUT; restore copies stored spec documents in api_specs.items without full extension admission (it only checks that each x-ferrum-proxy.plugins entry is an object with a string plugin_config_id), so a stale x-ferrum-* key inside a stored spec restores and is refused only when that spec is next submitted. The Edge #7520 and #7524 openapi.yaml changes add additionalProperties: false to Admin request bodies (the /mesh/egress-scope/test body, CreateNamespaceRequest, UpdateNamespaceRequest, AcmeCertificateRequest, AcmeOrderRequest, AcmeOrderFinalizeRequest, AcmeRenewRequest, ManagedTlsCertificateRequest, ManagedTlsCaBundleRequest, ManagedTlsCrlRequest, ManagedTlsOcspResponseRequest, ManagedTlsJwksRequest and TlsValidateRequest) and to nested proxy, upstream and trust objects (Proxy, PluginAssociation, CircuitBreakerConfig, RetryConfig and both backoff variants, GatewayTrustBundleSet, TrustBundle and its JWT authority items, Upstream, UpstreamTarget, SubsetDefinition, SubsetTrafficPolicy, MeshTrafficPolicyTls, UpstreamLocalityLbSetting, LocalityDistribute, LocalityFailover, BackendTlsConfig, TcpKeepaliveCfg, UpstreamPortOverride, HashOnCookieConfig, HealthCheckConfig, ActiveHealthCheck, PassiveHealthCheck, and ServiceDiscoveryConfig with its dns_sd, kubernetes, consul and mesh objects), remove PassiveHealthCheck.gateway_error_codes and PassiveHealthCheck.split_external_local_origin_errors (Edge #7520), and change the HealthResponse and BackupResponse ferrum_version examples to 1.0.0 (Edge #7531). Unreleased Admin API behavior in Edge #7491 outside plugin config schemas: confirm and confirm_api_spec_deletion are read with form-urlencoded decoding and fail closed when any repeated occurrence is not true (v0.9.21 accepted the flag if any occurrence was true); GET /metrics, GET /metrics/runtime and backup serialization return 500 on a serialization failure instead of 200 with an empty object; ACME order creation and renewal map upstream transport and ACME client errors, unusable finalization material and a terminally invalid order to 502, while request validation (including a CA authorization offering none of the requested challenge types) and egress-policy refusals still return 400; and the gateway trust-bundle record validator used by POST /restore applies the shared resource-ID rule (at most 254 bytes, an ASCII alphanumeric first, then alphanumerics, ., _ or -) where v0.9.21's record validator and openapi.yaml allowed 255 bytes with no character rule (explicit IDs on create already followed it). Unreleased API-spec admission rules outside plugin config schemas (Edge #7491): POST/PUT /api-specs reject non-object (positional) x-ferrum-plugins entries and the reserved $serde_json::private::RawValue key at any nesting depth in declared x-ferrum-plugins config subtrees or generated/merged x-ferrum-validate/x-ferrum-mcp configs with 400 MalformedExtension, and tighten external-$ref admission (500,000-node ceiling on external JSON -> 400 InvalidJson, 120-container document nesting cap -> 400 InvalidJson/InvalidYaml, 128 MiB normalized / 64 MiB compressed snapshot caps -> 422 SchemaTooLarge, and extending v0.9.21's disallowed-media-type allowlist with duplicate Content-Type rejection and full media-type/parameter syntax validation -> 422 SchemaReference for all three cases). The Edge #7491 openapi.yaml changes are Admin API alignments outside plugin config schemas: adding HEAD on /health, /live and /status, which at runtime now answer only GET and HEAD (v0.9.21 dispatched them on the path alone); adding components.responses.{ApiSpecReadServiceUnavailable, TlsRecordInUseConflict} and components.schemas.{TlsRecordInUseConflict, TlsRecordUsage, ValidationErrorResponse}; removing unused OverloadNoProxyState; tightening ApiSpecBackupItem (resource_hash required), ApiSpecSummary (required fields and representation-specific ETag description on content_hash), DeploymentSnapshot (explicit string types on api_specs[].id and api_specs[].proxy_id) and BackupResponse; and updating other non-plugin admin endpoint responses and descriptions (AcmeAccount, AcmeCertificateRequest, AcmeOrderFinalizeRequest, AdminMetricsGateway, AdminMetricsLoadBalancers, ApiSpecCreateResponse, ApiSpecParseError, ApiSpecValidationError, ClusterStatusDp, CredentialFingerprint, DatabaseDeltaPollingMetrics, GatewayTrustBundle, GatewayTrustBundleCreate, HealthResponse, ManagedTlsCaBundleRequest, ManagedTlsCertificateRequest, OverloadLevelOnly and TlsValidateResponse).
